body.reason: 'COX' is an abbreviation or symbol, not an enzyme name, and Caterva does not resolve one by itself; 2 enzymes go by it

candidates.name: cytochrome-c oxidase
candidates.why: COX is a common abbreviation for cytochrome-c oxidase and, as COX-1 and COX-2, cyclooxygenase; it is also used for other enzymes, so the choice is yours
candidates.reaction: 4 Fe(II)-[cytochrome c] + O2 + 8 H(+)(in) = 4 Fe(III)-[cytochrome c] + 2 H2O + 4 H(+)(out).
candidates.class_path: Translocases > catalysing the translocation of hydrons > hydron translocation or charge separation linked to oxidoreductase reactions

candidates.name: prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase
candidates.why: COX is a common abbreviation for cytochrome-c oxidase and, as COX-1 and COX-2, cyclooxygenase; it is also used for other enzymes, so the choice is yours
candidates.reaction: (5Z,8Z,11Z,14Z)-eicosatetraenoate + AH2 + 2 O2 = prostaglandin H2 + A + H2O.
candidates.class_path: Oxidoreductases > acting on paired donors, with incorporation or reduction of molecular oxygen. The oxygen incorporated need not be derived from O2 > miscellaneous
